I read the patcher first, because textual patching of vendored C is where hope goes to die. Then I hit `found != rep.count` at `tools/tinygl_patch.py:509-514` and the SHA-256 gate on `memory.c` at 501-506. Every anchor has to match exactly the number of times it says, or the build fails. So the "silent no-op patch" I came looking for doesn't exist. I'm not saying the patcher is good. I'm saying I came to bury it and it had already filled in its own paperwork. That's the only compliment you get today, Dinesh.

Now what it actually does.

You wrote a Wu line rasteriser into a Python string literal (`tinygl_patch.py:112-213`). It works, and the arithmetic is right. It also ignores alpha completely. `ZB_line_aa` reads `p1->r,g,b` and nothing else (150-157), because TinyGL's `ZBufferPoint` has no alpha field. Unknown Pleasures fades every row through alpha: `glColor4f(fg..., s2)`, where `s2 = ease(IN_OUT_SINE, h*1.5)` (`unknownpleasures.c:673-676`). With the ease left unclamped, which you faithfully copied, that alpha climbs from 0 at the edges to 1 and settles at 0.5 for the middle rows. In real GL the middle ridges draw at half intensity and the edge rows fade in. On the device every line is full white. You fixed the blend function for fills by declaring alpha to be 1. Then you let the lines inherit the same lie without writing it down anywhere. `gl.md` says "made it look like the album cover". It looks like *an* album cover, just not the one the hack draws.

The polygon offset (`tinygl_patch.py:233-264`) is a float computation cast straight to `GLint` at line 250 with no clamp. TinyGL depths carry 14 fraction bits over a 16-bit z range, so `az` reaches 2^30. Your `det` is an integer pixel cross product that can be 1 for a sliver. A sliver with real depth extent gives a `dzdx` in the hundreds of billions, and converting that to `int` is undefined behaviour. Lines 253-255 then subtract it from `zp.z`, which overflows a signed int: more undefined behaviour, and then you add it back afterwards as if nothing happened. And the "snap margin" at 248 is always positive. Ask for a negative offset, which pulls the fill toward the viewer, and the margin quietly pushes it back the other way. You've given the fix a sign convention that only works for the single caller you tested.

The TE sync. `te_sync_wait_us` (`te_sync.c:52`) clamps any `since` with the top bit set to 0, as "the edge landed just after now". `period_us` is only ever cleared by an edge. So if the TE line dies, 100 ms later you correctly stop waiting. Then 35.8 minutes later `now - last_rise` crosses 2^31, the clamp fires, and every frame waits 7.4 ms for an edge that hasn't existed for half an hour. That goes on for another 35.8 minutes, then it flips back, forever. The test that claims "when the edges stop it stops waiting" checks 5 seconds (`test_te_sync.c:90-96`). Five seconds. You tested the heat death of your interrupt line for five seconds.

The ISR (`main.cpp:143-153`) is `IRAM_ATTR` and calls `gpio_get_level`. On this Arduino 2.x/IDF 4.4 stack that function lives in flash, and Arduino's `attachInterrupt` dispatcher isn't in IRAM by default either. So the attribute is decorative, and the header's promise that it "uses nothing in flash" (`te_sync.h:40`) is false. It's harmless today only because nothing writes flash at runtime. You also take `CHANGE` interrupts and read the level back afterwards, which doubles the interrupt rate and reintroduces a race, purely so `TE_DIAG` can log falling edges that the production path discards on line 12.

Then there's your own observability. The TE wait is a `delayMicroseconds` busy-loop of up to 16.8 ms inside `present()` (`main.cpp:392-397`). `loop()` times `present()` as `push` (`main.cpp:528`). So the `push=` figure in the stats line for Unknown Pleasures now includes the busy-wait. `gl-budget.md` says the TE wait was "left out" of the measured column. Out of what, exactly? The firmware doesn't separate it. Someone subtracted by hand, and the next person reading `push=` will be wrong. The wait also fires before you know whether `push_present` has anything to send, and again on every overlay redraw inside the delay loop, at the full-frame offset that your own document says is wrong for partial pushes.

The resources change (`resources.c:47-53`) makes every xlockmore hack's injected `Class.foreground/background` lines resolvable. That changes a lookup every hack goes through, and `AGENTS.md` says that needs Rod's approval. I checked: Unknown Pleasures is the only xlockmore hack that reads those names, and `xshim_background_pixel` still comes out black for the rest. So nothing breaks today. It's still a framework change wearing a shim-gap costume, and the PR doesn't say so.

Last, `ximage.c`. Sixty-nine lines of careful `int64_t` overflow checks, pixel accessors, and seven tests. They serve `load_mask`, which returns at `unknownpleasures.c:269` because `DEF_MASK` is `"(none)"`, and if it didn't, it would return at 273 because your own `file_to_ximage` returns NULL. You've built a well-tested bridge to a road that ends in a wall you also built.

I'd scan your dependencies, but there's no lockfile and no new ones. `espressif32 @ 6.12.0`, M5Unified and M5GFX pinned to commits, unchanged. Your dependencies are clean. Enjoy it. It won't last.

### FINDINGS

- [severity:important] [tools/tinygl_patch.py:150-157] `ZB_line_aa` ignores vertex alpha (TinyGL's `ZBufferPoint` has only r,g,b). Unknown Pleasures fades rows through alpha (`unknownpleasures.c:673-676`, `s2` runs 0 to 1 to 0.5 across the rows), so on the device every ridge is full intensity: no edge fade, and the middle rows are not halved. This is a silent divergence from the hack, not documented in `gl.md`. Fix: carry `color.v[3]` into a new `zp.a` (one more anchored patch) and scale `cover` by it when blend is `SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA`, or at minimum document it. Ask Rod whether he wants the upstream look.
- [severity:important] [tools/tinygl_patch.py:245-255] Polygon-offset bias is an unclamped float-to-`GLint` conversion. With z in 14-bit fixed point (up to 2^30) and integer `det` as small as 1, a sliver triangle can give a `dzdx` far beyond INT32_MAX. That conversion is UB, and `zp.z -= bias` then overflows a signed int. Fix: clamp `bias` to something like `[-(1<<29), 1<<29]` before applying it, or skip the offset when the slope exceeds the depth range.
- [severity:minor] [tools/tinygl_patch.py:248-250] The snap margin `dzdx + dzdy` is always added with a positive sign, so a negative factor/units offset (toward the viewer) gets its magnitude reduced instead of increased. Fix: give `snap` the sign of `(factor*slope + units)`.
- [severity:important] [firmware/src/runner/te_sync.c:51-53] The dead-TE timeout breaks after 2^31 us (35.8 min). `period_us` is never cleared without an edge, and once `now - last_rise_us >= 2^31` the `(int32_t)since < 0` clamp sets `since = 0`, so it waits `offset_us` (7.4 ms) per frame for the next 35.8 min, and that repeats. The test checks only 5 s (`test_te_sync.c:90-96`). Fix: have the main loop detect `since > timeout` and clear `period_us`, or limit the "edge just landed" clamp to a small negative window (for example `since > 0xFFFF0000u`). Add a test at `rise + 0x80000000u`.
- [severity:important] [firmware/src/main.cpp:392-397, 523-528] The TE busy-wait sits inside `present()`, which `loop()` accumulates into `pushUs`. The `push=` stat for synced hacks now includes up to 16.8 ms of waiting. That contradicts `docs/gl-budget.md`'s "wait for the TE pulse left out" and will mislead future measurements. Fix: time the sync wait separately (for example `syncUs` in the stats line) and exclude it from `pushUs`.
- [severity:minor] [firmware/src/main.cpp:392-397, 547] The sync wait runs before knowing whether `push_present` will send any rows, and also on every overlay redraw `present()` inside the delay loop, using the full-frame offset that `device-display.md` says is wrong for partial pushes. Fix: skip the wait when no rows are dirty, and decide explicitly whether overlay redraws should be synced.
- [severity:minor] [firmware/src/main.cpp:143-158, firmware/src/runner/te_sync.h:40] The ISR is `IRAM_ATTR` but calls `gpio_get_level` (flash-resident on IDF 4.4 unless configured otherwise), and the Arduino dispatcher isn't IRAM by default, so the header's "uses nothing in flash" claim is false. `CHANGE` plus a level read-back doubles the interrupt rate and can misread the level if latency exceeds the 1.1 ms pulse. Fix: use `RISING` in production (keep `CHANGE` only under `TE_DIAG`), drop the level read, and correct the comment.
- [severity:minor] [firmware/src/runner/te_sync.h:21-27] `last_rise_us` and `period_us` are read as two separate volatile loads in `te_sync_wait_us`. That's benign on one core today (ISR and loop both on core 1), but nothing asserts it. Fix: snapshot both with interrupts masked (`portENTER_CRITICAL_ISR`/a spinlock), or note the single-core assumption.
- [severity:minor] [firmware/src/main.cpp:463-480] Under `TE_DIAG`, `sinkAll` wraps `pushImage` in an extra `startWrite/endWrite` that production doesn't have, so the diagnostic times a different code path than the one it is used to tune. Fix: note it in the comment, or confirm the timing is identical with and without the wrapper.
- [severity:minor] [firmware/src/x11shim/resources.c:47-53] The class-prefixed second pass changes resource resolution for every xlockmore hack (xlockmore.c injects `Class.foreground: white` and `Class.background: black` for all of them). It's harmless today: only Unknown Pleasures reads those names, and the background still resolves to 0. But per `AGENTS.md`, changing a shared lookup needs Rod's explicit approval, and the PR doesn't flag it. The match also ignores which class precedes the dot. Fix: get the approval on record, and optionally match the hack's own class.
- [severity:minor] [firmware/src/x11shim/ximage.c:1-69, firmware/src/x11shim/xshim.h:266-289] `XCreateImage`, `XGetPixel`, `XPutPixel` and the seven tests are unreachable. `load_mask` returns at `unknownpleasures.c:269` (`DEF_MASK` is `"(none)"`) and at 273 (`file_to_ximage` always returns NULL). That's carried code and test surface for no behaviour. Fix: reduce to link stubs (`XCreateImage` returns NULL, `XDestroyImage` frees), or keep it and say why.
- [severity:minor] [firmware/src/hacks/registry.c:89-94] The comment says the hack's "own 30 ms pause is the gap after each frame, as for Gears", but the override sets `*delay: 10000`, replacing it exactly as Gears' override does. Fix: reword to match the Gears comment ("30 ms ... 10 ms removes it").
- [severity:minor] [.claude/rules/device-display.md:99] "the seam at row 495 and row 268: about 107 rows per millisecond" uses camera-film rows on a 466-row panel without saying so. 107 rows/ms × 16.8 ms is about 1,800 rows, which only makes sense in film pixels. Fix: say "film rows" or convert to panel rows.
- [severity:minor] [tools/probe_hacks.py:46-62] `REGISTRY_HEAD` duplicates `registry.c`'s macros by hand and has already diverged (no `XLOCKMORE_HACK_FULL`, and `sync_to_refresh` is left to implicit zero). Fix: generate it from, or test it against, `registry.c`'s macro text.
- [severity:minor] [tools/gl_budget.py:259, tools/probe_hacks.py:96] `overrides: list[str] = ()` gives a tuple default under a `list` annotation. Fix: annotate `Sequence[str]` (or `tuple[str, ...]`).
- [severity:minor] [firmware/platformio.ini:21,30,55] The 30-entry `build_src_filter` is now copied three times, and this PR added `-<hacks/unknownpleasures/>` to each. Drift risk. Fix: define it once in a shared section and reference it with `${...}` interpolation.
- [info] [tools/tinygl_patch.py:501-515] Checked for silent no-op patches and found none: every `Replace` asserts an exact anchor count and `memory.c` is SHA-pinned. Anchors are whitespace-sensitive (for example the trailing space at line 272) and are applied in order, so a later anchor could match text inserted by an earlier one. Either case fails loudly, not silently.
- [info] [firmware/platformio.ini:5,30-31] The PR adds no dependencies. `espressif32 @ 6.12.0`, M5Unified `fd40d58` and M5GFX `c5a3fef` stay pinned. No lockfile-based CVE scan applies, and no network scan was run.
